description:
## Outcome

The coding pack supplies replaceable `write` and exact `edit` operations. Each successful mutation returns a portable edit record and environment checkpoint reference.

## Why now

Mutation follows proven read boundaries and durable checkpoints. The edit record gives the CLI a review surface without a second mutation state.

## Current state

No mutation tools exist. The execution lifecycle can now checkpoint and recover workspace state. The read tool can supply digests. Jidoka policy can require allow or review before an external effect.

## Ownership and boundary

This is a `jidoka` built-in extension change. Mutations occur only in a write-capable constrained environment and pass host policy. The CLI later renders edit records; it does not implement writes or undo.

## Detailed implementation

1. Register `coding.write` and `coding.edit` with typed inputs and separate permission classes.
2. `write` creates or replaces a bounded regular file only under explicit trusted overwrite policy and optional expected-before digest.
3. `edit` uses exact text match with expected occurrence count and optional before digest. On conflict it writes nothing.
4. Use safe atomic replacement when the backend supports it and report the confirmed write method.
5. Checkpoint before mutation and return path, before/after digest, size, operation ID, summary, bounded diff data, and checkpoint/undo reference.
6. Recheck canonical path and ignore policy at mutation time.
7. On interruption or partial backend error, report confirmed final state and preserve recovery evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Create, guarded overwrite, and exact edit work in a write-capable profile.
- [ ] Count mismatch, digest conflict, path denial, or policy denial makes no change.
- [ ] Every success returns a portable edit record and checkpoint reference.
- [ ] No host write occurs without confirmed write enforcement.
- [ ] Cancellation or failure reports whether the workspace changed and supports recovery.
- [ ] Both tools can be disabled or replaced independently.

## Test plan

- Success: create, replace with digest, one-match edit, multi-match expected count, and checkpoint restore.
- Invalid input: empty path, outside root, ignored target, bad count, oversized content, and digest mismatch.
- Runtime failure: interrupted write, disk full, rename failure, checkpoint failure, and cleanup failure.
- Boundary and security: policy review/deny, symlink swap, read-only profile, and no edit record secret content.
- Deterministic capability: fake execution environment, workspace, checkpoint, policy, clock, and IDs.
- JSONL and exit status: projected edit/error/checkpoint data is portable for later case results.

## Documentation

Document exact-match rules, overwrite guards, edit records, checkpoints, recovery, limits, and replace/disable configuration.

## Non-goals

Do not add arbitrary patch languages, source control commits, automatic acceptance, or TUI rendering. Do not write directly on the host outside the execution port.

## Dependencies

Blocking issues:

- `jido_cli-tqg.5.2` — Add removable read and search coding tools
- `jido_cli-tqg.3.5` — Persist portable execution bindings through recovery and fork

Features unlocked by this story:

- Interactive edit review
- Checkpoint-backed coding changes
- Git diff verification after edits

## Commit plan

Create exactly one focused `jidoka` commit. Use a message such as `feat(jidoka): add reviewed coding edits (jido_cli-tqg.5.3)`. Do not include another backlog feature.

## Verification commands

```sh
cd /Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_cli/jidoka
mix test test/jidoka/coding_pack/write_test.exs test/jidoka/coding_pack/edit_test.exs test/integration/coding_pack_checkpoint_integration_test.exs
mix quality
mix test
mix docs
```
title: Add reviewed write and exact-edit coding tools
